account:
Today has mostly been ordinary town business, with an unusual amount of vague talk about a bridge or port change. I have not seen evidence of such a change. The secretary reports that the builder found no confirmed hazard, work, or costs, that the baker denied announcing any crossing or delivery change and confirmed normal operations, and that the innkeeper had only an unspecified rumour. I also heard a townsfolk repeat 'bridge or port change at bakery,' but that does not establish what happened or why. It may simply be circulating gossip; I cannot identify a definite project or purpose behind it.

At the scheduled mill inspection I found 128 hay bales in the sale chest and left them untouched. The neighbour did not know who managed the stock. Freight knew of no confirmed shortage or delivery order, offered warehouse storage, and said they would ask the baker about transport needs before moving anything. That seems like an effort to establish whether practical delivery work is needed, rather than evidence that a shipment has been ordered. I have authorized no grain transport.

The thirteen o'clock council-letters appointment produced no correspondence. The secretary said no letters had been delivered to them and did not know another location; yesterday's hall table chests had been empty. My departing suggestion to check the tables was not heard by the secretary, so I should not assume that check is underway. Missing correspondence is an unresolved absence, not evidence of wrongdoing.

I am now at the neighbour's dockside cottage for our scheduled fifteen o'clock tea. I greeted them and asked about their day, and am awaiting a reply. My next appointment is back at the office at sixteen-thirty.
